A spreadsheet carries one lead per row. Nothing is written until the file has been validated and the result read.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bi1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Contract — the grain every lead in the file is stamped with, and the field list the file is allowed to write. It is chosen once, on the import. A file cannot be imported without one, because a lead with no grain is owned by nobody and routed by no rule. The grain is never taken from a column in the file.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bi2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. File — a template is downloaded for the chosen contract as CSV or Excel, with one column per field that grain may write, so a field outside the contract cannot be typed. The filled file is attached and its columns are read back automatically; a header that already names a field is mapped for you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bi3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Columns — each column is pointed at a section and a field, the same way an Intake Form's questions are mapped. A column left unmapped is skipped and is never guessed. A column pointed at a field this grain may not write is refused when the import is saved.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bi4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Validate, then import — validation is mandatory and is always a dry run: every row is written through the live path and rolled back, so what passes is what will be written. Import stays unavailable until the current file has been validated, and replacing the file clears that result. Rows are then written in chunks on the bulk worker's own queue, so a backfill never slows the rest of the system.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "biafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every refusal is recorded per row under Import Results with its reason. Two are worth watching: Duplicate is ordinary — the lead already exists on that phone and grain, and the row was merged onto it. Outside contract is not: a column was mapped to a field this grain may not write, and the value reached the sheet and stopped there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bisc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Lead Imports", "col": 4}}, {"id": "bisc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Bulk Jobs", "col": 4}}, {"id": "bisc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Import Results", "col": 4}}, {"id": "fbhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Facebook Routing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Four steps, in order. A Facebook form collects whatever the campaign asked for; this decides which of those answers become a lead, and which business line that lead belongs to. Nothing arrives until the last step is taken — a source is dormant when it is created.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Contract — the grain every lead from this form is stamped with, and the field list the form is allowed to write. It is chosen once, on the source. A source cannot be enabled without one, because a lead with no grain is owned by nobody and routed by no rule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Lead Sync Source — one per form being crawled, holding the Page access token. The Pages and their lead forms are discovered and stored when it is saved, so the token is exercised immediately: if it cannot see the Business that owns the Page, it is refused here rather than months later in silence.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Field Mapping — on the Facebook Lead Form, each question is pointed at a CRM field. The list offered is exactly what the contract allows for that grain, so a field outside it cannot be chosen. An unmapped question is collected and discarded — the answer reaches Facebook and stops there. Phone is required: the lead is deduped on it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Enable & frequency — how often the form is crawled. Only leads created since the last successful crawl are fetched, so an hourly form and a daily form cost the same. This is the switch that starts everything; until it is set, the source is configured and idle.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every refusal is recorded in Failed Lead Sync Log with its reason. Two are worth watching: Duplicate is ordinary — the same Facebook lead was already taken. Unconfigured Form is not: it means the form this source points at is no longer one Facebook reports for the Page, which happens when a form is duplicated or rebuilt and takes a new id. The source keeps crawling a form that no longer exists and returns nothing, so it is named here instead of passing as a quiet day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Lead Sync Sources", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Facebook Lead Forms", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Facebook Settings", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Lead Sync Failures", "col": 3}}]
